title: Identity normalization of compact-support refinement components
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $\Lambda$ be an admissible condensed commutative ring object [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism. For every scheme-theoretically dense boundary compactification $c$ of $f$ [def-sf-comp-refinement-data] and every unbounded derived $\Lambda_X$-module object $K$, the canonical component $\rho_{1_c}(K)$ of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] is the identity of $Rp_*D(j_!)K$, where $c=(j,p)$. Here $\rho$ uses the open-refinement map of [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement] and the derived module direct-image compositor induced by [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. No localizing-membership hypothesis on $K$ is required.

source.place: Proof, refinement isomorphisms, identity normalization (DAG step 4); Stacks Tag 0D6E

proof.text: Apply the identity clause of localizingRefinement_coherence in the stated geometric/coefficient setting, to the given dense compactification and arbitrary unbounded K. Cancel the derived identity isomorphism to express localizingRefinementMap(identity) as its inverse.

Prove the generic total right-derived left unit law with rightDerived_ext. The factorization equation of mapDerivedCategoryIdIso and naturality of the derived-functor unit express the derived identity inverse on Qh(K). The composition comparison factorization then reduces to the underived left unit equation. Apply this with lowerStar(identity), lowerStar(p), the module identity identification and lowerStarComp_id_left. Substitute the open-refinement identity into compactificationRefinementComponent to obtain map(identity inverse) followed by the derived compositor and transport; the generic unit law gives identity.

proof_origin.note: Identity part of det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle step 4, proved from the already stated dense open-refinement identity and the generic derived-functor universal property.

from.place: Proof (3), canonical comparisons from det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle; identity refinement normalization in that node proof step 4

theorem compactificationRefinementComponent_id
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (hΛ : IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ℓ Λ)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f)
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))) :
    compactificationRefinementComponent Λ (𝟙 c.obj) K = 𝟙 _
